def manhattan_distance_int(x1, y1, x2, y2):
    """Picture two points on a city grid where you can only walk along the
    streets, never diagonally. You start at (x1, y1) and want to get to
    (x2, y2), so the walking distance is simply how far you go sideways
    plus how far you go up or down. All four arguments are ints. Figure
    out the horizontal gap, figure out the vertical gap, and add the two
    together. Return abs(x1 - x2) + abs(y1 - y2) exactly. There are no
    square roots and nothing to round here — this is the taxicab flavor
    of distance, and the arithmetic stays in plain whole numbers from
    start to finish.

    >>> manhattan_distance_int(0, 0, 0, 0)
    0
    >>> manhattan_distance_int(1, 2, 4, 6)
    7
    """
